Mortality data observed at any granularity

Source: R/data-mt_data.R
mt_data.Rd

mt_data() stores death counts, exposures (person-years at risk) and populations for one or more strata. Each table may use its own age and period resolution, for example deaths in 5-year age groups with an open 90+ interval and exposures in single years of age. The container keeps the observations as they were supplied; harmonisation onto a common grid happens explicitly with mt_regroup() and mt_ungroup().

Usage

mt_data(
  deaths = NULL,
  exposure = NULL,
  population = NULL,
  by = NULL,
  age = "age",
  period = "year",
  value = NULL,
  age_open = NULL,
  omega = 110,
  missing = c(".", "..", "...", ":", "x", "X", "/", "NA", ""),
  zero = "-",
  decimal = "."
)

Arguments

deaths, exposure, population

Data frames in long format, one row per cell, or NULL.

by

Character vector of stratum columns (for example "sex").

age

Age column: one column with single ages (numeric) or labels such as "30-34" and "90+" (see parse_age_labels()), or two columns with the lower and upper bound (Inf for an open interval).

period

Period column: calendar years (numeric), labels such as "2010-2014", or two columns with lower and upper bounds.

value

Name of the value column. Either one name used for all tables, or a named vector or list such as c(deaths = "D", exposure = "E"). By default the column named after the measure, otherwise "value". A table in wide format, with one value column per level of a stratum variable (for example columns Female and Male, or one column per cause of death), is read by giving all its value columns, for example value = list(deaths = c(female = "Female", male = "Male")): the columns become the levels (named by the names of the vector, else the column names) of the one variable in by that the table lacks.

age_open

Lower bound of an open age interval coded as a single numeric age (for example 110 for the Human Mortality Database "110+").

omega

Assumed maximum age, used wherever an open interval needs a finite upper bound.

missing

Values that mark missing cells in character value columns, for example the symbols of official statistics for confidential or unknown counts (".", "x"). Missing cells are left out; suppressed death counts can then be estimated with mt_fill_suppressed().

zero

Values that mark a count of zero (for example "-").

decimal

Decimal mark of values given as text: "." (thousands separators such as "12,345" are recognised) or "," (as in many European exports: "1.234,5").

Value

An object of class mt_data.

Details

Age labels of many sources are recognised (see parse_age_labels()); periods are years, ranges of years or financial years ("2001/02"). Rows whose age or period is labelled as a total ("All ages", "Total", "Insgesamt") are left out with a warning. Values of unknown age ("Unknown", "not stated", "unbekannt") are distributed over the age groups of the same stratum and period in proportion to the known values, the usual practice of the Human Mortality Database, with a warning. Leading and trailing spaces in stratum labels are removed; rows without a stratum label are left out. A warning lists levels of a stratum variable that occur in one table only (for example "F" in one table and "female" in another).

A table may leave out stratum columns over which its values are shared. For example, deaths by region, sex and cause of death and populations by region and sex: every cause of death then uses the population of its region and sex. Tables with all stratum columns are read first and define the strata.

See also

mt_add_deaths(), mt_grid(), mt_regroup(), mt_ungroup(), as_mt_data().

Examples

d <- data.frame(sex = "female", year = 2001:2002, age = "90+",
                deaths = c(120, 130), exposure = c(800, 820))
mt_data(deaths = d, exposure = d, by = "sex")
#> <mt_data> 1 stratum by sex, omega = 110
#>   deaths     open interval 90+; periods 2001-2002 (width 1); 2 cells
#>   exposure   open interval 90+; periods 2001-2002 (width 1); 2 cells
#>   grid       <mt_axis: age, 1 interval> 90+
#>              <mt_axis: period, 2 intervals> 2001 2002
